extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit organizations, researchers, policymakers, and practitioners seeking grants from Carnegie Corporation of New York
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes Carnegie Corporation of New York's programmatic priorities and the kinds of work it funds across Education, U.S. Democracy, and International Program areas. Useful for prospective applicants aligning proposals with Carnegie's objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education — access to learning leading to meaningful careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grantmaking helps students of all ages and backgrounds access learning that leads to meaningful careers, upward mobility, and civic participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on programs or interventions that expand equitable access to learning across ages and backgrounds, and that have clear pathways to employment, economic mobility, and engagement in civic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education — support social cohesion and trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Education works to support the forces of cohesion that build trust in public institutions, reduce political polarization, and strengthen our democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to education-related work that also fosters societal cohesion — e.g., initiatives that reduce polarization, build trust in institutions, or promote democratic norms and civic skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy — nonpartisan organizations reducing political polarization
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie’s Strengthening U.S. Democracy program supports nonpartisan organizations that are working to reduce political polarization in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be nonpartisan and demonstrate how their work materially addresses polarization and contributes to healthier democratic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy — focus area: elections and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives focused on elections and governance are a core area of focus for Carnegie’s democracy work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects improving the integrity, accessibility, or functioning of elections and governance structures align with this focus area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy — focus area: state community service
rubrics_metrics.description: State community service is named as a priority initiative within the democracy program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs that expand service at the state level, connect citizens to civic action, or strengthen civic infrastructure fit this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy — focus area: universal civic learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal civic learning is an explicit area of initiative for strengthening democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational efforts that ensure broad-based civic knowledge, skills, and dispositions for participation are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy — focus area: legal immigration pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal immigration pathways are listed as a targeted area of Carnegie’s democracy investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that improves or expands lawful immigration pathways and integrates immigration policy into democratic resiliency is relevant here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy — bringing people together across differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie continues to make investments in opportunities to bring people together to solve problems across differences, including core grantees such as the Trust for Civic Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should show how they convene or create sustained opportunities for cross-difference problem-solving and community bridging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy — support for research, convenings, and public education
rubrics_metrics.description: Across these areas of focus, Carnegie supports research, convenings, public education, and other activities aimed at strengthening American democracy and public trust in government and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects delivering rigorous research, high-quality convenings, public education campaigns, or other demonstrable activities that bolster democratic institutions and trust are of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Program — advancing peace broadly defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grantmaking is guided by Andrew Carnegie’s founding vision: to advance peace as both the absence of armed conflict and the creation of conditions that sustain nonviolent growth and change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding preference for work that pursues both conflict reduction and the structural conditions that support lasting, nonviolent development and peaceful change.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Program — focus area: preventing and managing conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Program focuses on preventing and managing conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that demonstrate capacity to prevent escalation, manage ongoing conflicts, or create durable conflict-mitigation mechanisms align with this priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Program — focus area: movements of people
rubrics_metrics.description: One area of focus is movements of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work addressing displacement, migration flows, protection, integration, or policy responses related to population movements is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Program — focus area: non-state actors
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Program focuses on non-state actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives that engage, analyze, or influence the role of non-state actors (e.g., civil society, militias, transnational groups) in peace and policy landscapes are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Program — emphasize policy-relevant research, institutions, impact, and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Together, these priorities reflect Carnegie’s commitment to fostering policy-relevant research, strengthening institutions and practices, impacting lives, and amplifying voices to shape more peaceful futures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for proposals that are policy-relevant, strengthen institutional capacity or practice, have measurable impact on people’s lives, and elevate marginalized or important voices in pursuit of peace.
